key_insight: BudgetMem trains a query-aware routing policy that dynamically directs queries to different memory tiers at runtime, letting agents retrieve and store only the information that matters under an explicit compute/latency budget.
problem_solved: Replaces inefficient, query-agnostic offline memory construction (which can waste resources or drop query-critical facts) with a controllable, runtime mechanism that balances task performance against cost.
method: Multi-tier runtime memory architecture: organize memories into budgeted tiers (e.g., hot/near/long-term) with different access costs and retention properties.
Learned query-aware routing: a policy predicts which tier(s) to access or update for each query, conditioned on an explicit budget constraint.
Budget-conditioned optimization: train the router with a cost-aware objective (or RL) to trade off accuracy vs. latency/compute and provide explicit control over resource usage.
impact: Makes LLM agents more efficient and reliable in long-horizon or multi-session settings by improving task accuracy under constrained compute/latency and giving practitioners direct control over the performance–cost trade-off.
visual_elements: Tiered memory diagram: stacked layers (hot/near/long-term) with arrows showing query routing decisions and differing cost icons.
Routing policy flowchart: query → router → selected memory tier(s) → response, with budget input controlling routing.
Performance vs. cost curve: plot showing improved accuracy (or utility) as a function of compute/latency budget for BudgetMem vs. offline baselines.
Example timeline: agent interaction timeline highlighting which memories were stored/retrieved per step and how routing adapts to query importance.
paper_title: Learning Query-Aware Budget-Tier Routing for Runtime Agent Memory
paper_authors: Haozhen Zhang, Haodong Yue, Tao Feng, Quanyu Long, Jianzhu Bao
